claims.text: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response under magnetic and pressure fields.
The unmodified alloy has poor structural integrity and is prone to cracking under operational loads.
A minor low-melting metal or alloy component can form an in-situ intergranular binder phase during processing.
The introduced binder phase will self-assemble into a continuous network along the alloy's grain boundaries.
The intergranular binder network will be ductile and highly thermally conductive.
The binder will fill intergranular spaces and reinforce the matrix.
The binder network will alleviate stress concentrations at grain boundaries.
Alleviating grain-boundary stress concentrations will inhibit crack initiation and propagation.
The binder's high thermal conductivity will improve heat transport during caloric phase transformations.
The binder network will not interfere materially with the phase transformation responsible for the caloric response.
The modified alloy will have significantly greater compressive strength than the unchanged alloy.
The modified alloy can attain a compressive strength of approximately 200 MPa or greater.
The modified alloy will retain its large caloric response with only a minimal reduction in response magnitude.
The mechanical and caloric benefits will persist under magnetic-field and pressure-field operation in the original temperature and loading regimes.
Excessive binder volume fraction may disrupt the beneficial effects or caloric phase transformation.
Performance may deteriorate when operating conditions exceed the optimized processing window.
